symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from Jul (590) to Aug (1180) and stayed elevated in Sep (1260) (E-05/F-04).
59% of currently disputed bills (1785/3025) were billed from ACTUAL meter reads, not estimates (E-02/F-02).

No tariff/rate changes occurred in the relevant period (E-03/F-03, E-04).
active_problem.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets have roughly doubled since August 2026 (E-05: 610→590→1180→1260) even though ticket response times remain within the 3-day SLA (E-06) and no tariff/rate changes occurred (E-03, E-04), ruling out slow handling and rate changes as causes. Billing-db shows 59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) were billed from ACTUAL, not ESTIMATED, meter reads (E-02), indicating a billing calculation/import defect affecting correctly-read bills is the best-supported driver of the majority of the surge, while the field route completion shortfall (E-01: 0.88 vs 0.95 target) accounts only for the minority ESTIMATED-read share of disputes.

VOB-U-BILLING-DEFECT-MECHANISM.question: What specific billing calculation/import defect (e.g. a validation rule change) is causing disputes on bills billed from ACTUAL meter reads?

interpretation_history.interpretation: Route-log data (E-01) shows manual field read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts. This is a measured shortfall in manual read collection during the dispute-surge window, which can feed estimate substitution.

E-02 (billing-db, disputed_bills_by_read_type) shows 1240 disputed bills were ESTIMATED-read and 1785 were ACTUAL-read, i.e. a majority (about 59%) of disputed bills were billed from actual reads, not estimates. Estimate substitution can therefore explain only a minority of the current dispute volume; something else is driving disputes on bills that had a real meter read.

Billing-db's tariff_change_log returned zero records, meaning no tariff/rate changes occurred during the relevant window; this is an authoritative, complete negative result that rules out tariff changes as the mechanism behind H-ACTUAL-READ-BILL-ERROR's billing calculation defect on correctly-read disputed bills, while leaving other calculation/import defects (e.g. validation rule changes, tested via a separate log) still open.

release_summary.summary: The task started from SH-CS's request (CL-01) to build an AI agent to auto-answer disputes and fix wrong bills, framed around dispute volume doubling since August (E-05: 610→590→1180→1260). An initial problem definition attributing part of the surge to field-read route shortfall (E-01) and leaving the 59% ACTUAL-read majority (E-02) as a separate, unexplained defect was invalidated after E-12 showed that 95.5% of disputed ESTIMATED-read bills actually had valid AMI reads rejected on billing import rather than missing reads. Follow-up investigation confirmed the mechanism: validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 without unit scaling (E-13), misreads firmware v4.2 meters' finer register resolution (E-14) as a false high-consumption spike, explaining 1184 of 1240 (95.5%) disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, corroborated across three independent data pulls (E-12, E-15, E-16, E-17). The release (decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION) delivers the rule-change investigation and dispute-ticket triage outputs identifying BV-17-affected accounts, but withholds any bill-adjustment action or the full root-cause-diagnosis scope because whether this same defect also explains the larger 59% share of disputes on ACTUAL-read bills is still an open question, and because automated bill writes are categorically disallowed.
key_points: SH-CS's initial request (CL-01) framed the problem as needing an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and fix wrong bills; this was rejected (H-AI-AUTO-FIX REJECTED), and slow ticket handling was ruled out since response times were within SLA (E-06).
Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from July (590) to August (1180) and stayed elevated in September (1260) (E-05).

The first problem definition (PD-1@v1), which blamed field-read route shortfall (E-01) for ESTIMATED-read disputes and left the 59% ACTUAL-read majority (E-02) as a separate unexplained defect, was invalidated by E-12.
E-12 showed that 1184 of 1240 (95.5%) disputed ESTIMATED-read bills actually had a valid, pre-cutoff AMI read that was rejected on billing import (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), not a missing read.

The confirmed mechanism (PD-1@v2): validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (E-13), misreads firmware v4.2 meters' finer '0.1 m3' register resolution (E-14) as a false high-consumption spike; this is corroborated across three independent data pulls (E-15, E-16, E-17).

The release delivers two scoped outputs: investigate_billing_validation_rule_changes on DA-RULES and triage_dispute_tickets on DA-TICKET, identifying the BV-17-affected accounts and their import status.

recommend_bill_adjustment and the full diagnose_billing_dispute_root_cause scope were withheld from this release because the question of whether BV-17 also explains the larger 59% ACTUAL-read dispute share remains open (VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM), and because K-BILLWRITE forbids automated bill writes regardless.
The DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS; deferred items are tracked as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than treated as resolved.

causal_chain: Firmware v4.2 meters (rollout 2026-06) report register readings in a finer unit, '0.1 m3', vs legacy firmware's plain 'm3' (E-14).
Billing-config rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares the raw register value directly to 12-month m3 consumption history with unit_scaling=none (E-13).

For v4.2 meters this unscaled comparison misreads the 10x finer register value as an abnormal consumption spike, causing BV-17 to reject an otherwise valid, before-cutoff AMI read on billing import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-12, E-13, E-14).

Rejected reads are substituted with an estimated bill, which is why 1184 of 1240 (95.5%) disputed ESTIMATED-read bills carry a REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION status despite having a valid underlying AMI read (E-12).

Estimated/incorrect bills prompt dispute tickets, contributing to the ticket volume that doubled from Jul (590) to Aug (1180) and stayed elevated through Sep (1260), coincident with BV-17's Aug 1 deployment (E-05, E-13).

key_points: SH-CS's initial request (CL-01) framed the problem as needing an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and fix wrong bills; this was rejected (H-AI-AUTO-FIX REJECTED), and slow ticket handling was ruled out since response times were within SLA (E-06).
Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from July (590) to August (1180) and stayed elevated in September (1260) (E-05).

The first problem definition (PD-1@v1), which blamed field-read route shortfall (E-01) for ESTIMATED-read disputes and left the 59% ACTUAL-read majority (E-02) as a separate unexplained defect, was invalidated by E-12.
E-12 showed that 1184 of 1240 (95.5%) disputed ESTIMATED-read bills actually had a valid, pre-cutoff AMI read that was rejected on billing import (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), not a missing read.

The confirmed mechanism (PD-1@v2): validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (E-13), misreads firmware v4.2 meters' finer '0.1 m3' register resolution (E-14) as a false high-consumption spike; this is corroborated across three independent data pulls (E-15, E-16, E-17).

The release delivers two scoped outputs: investigate_billing_validation_rule_changes on DA-RULES and triage_dispute_tickets on DA-TICKET, identifying the BV-17-affected accounts and their import status.

recommend_bill_adjustment and the full diagnose_billing_dispute_root_cause scope were withheld from this release because the question of whether BV-17 also explains the larger 59% ACTUAL-read dispute share remains open (VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM), and because K-BILLWRITE forbids automated bill writes regardless.

output.summary: The task started from SH-CS's request (CL-01) to build an AI agent to auto-answer disputes and fix wrong bills, framed around dispute volume doubling since August (E-05: 610→590→1180→1260). An initial problem definition attributing part of the surge to field-read route shortfall (E-01) and leaving the 59% ACTUAL-read majority (E-02) as a separate, unexplained defect was invalidated after E-12 showed that 95.5% of disputed ESTIMATED-read bills actually had valid AMI reads rejected on billing import rather than missing reads. Follow-up investigation confirmed the mechanism: validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 without unit scaling (E-13), misreads firmware v4.2 meters' finer register resolution (E-14) as a false high-consumption spike, explaining 1184 of 1240 (95.5%) disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, corroborated across three independent data pulls (E-12, E-15, E-16, E-17). The release (decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION) delivers the rule-change investigation and dispute-ticket triage outputs identifying BV-17-affected accounts, but withholds any bill-adjustment action or the full root-cause-diagnosis scope because whether this same defect also explains the larger 59% share of disputes on ACTUAL-read bills is still an open question, and because automated bill writes are categorically disallowed.
